author_adjudication.consequence: no label normalisation is applied. Source-credit labels remain the strings the corpus carries, and no identity merging is performed.
author_adjudication.determination: all reviewed pairs are collaborations; no pair names one person twice
author_adjudication.not_evidence_of: that the labels are verified distinct people. The determination is that the corpus contains no detectable split of one credit across two strings, which is a narrower statement.
author_adjudication.reviewed: every candidate pair at or above a 10% mutual involvement share

privacy: aggregate only; label strings and counts, no lyric text or song identifiers
question: Whether any two source-credit labels name one artist, which would make a correct retrieval count as wrong and would hide duplicate records from PD-002's within-label control.

shared_passage_evidence.reading: One artist split across two strings would show near-total mutual overlap, because the same songs were filed twice. Partial overlap with both sides retaining songs the other lacks is collaboration.

string_similarity.verdict: unusable. No pair is identical after normalisation, and every substring candidate is a common stage-name particle -- applying such a rule would merge distinct artists.
